A Forbes analysis framed the situation as a genuine test of whether AI valuations have entered bubble territory, noting that Anthropic’s economics differ meaningfully from traditional software companies: usage drives both revenue and substantial operating expense simultaneously, given the enormous compute costs required to actually run frontier AI models at scale. That dynamic raises real questions about sustainable [...] Would its rapid revenue growth justify a $2 trillion valuation for Anthropic, or is it another sign that AI valuations have moved too far, too fast? At nine years old, Daniel Anstandig made the kind of pitch that does not need a deck. He called radio and television stations around Cleveland and offered to do anything. He would mop the floors. He would clean the toilets. He only wanted to come inside and learn. A family-owned station in Willoughby, Ohio, gave him the opening. The future founder of an artificial intelligence company began with the oldest apprenticeship in business: make yourself useful, then pay attention. # Daniel Anstandig Has Spent a Career Teaching Old Media New Moves

He started in a small Ohio radio station at nine. Now the Futuri founder is betting that the useful future of AI belongs to operators who listen before they automate. [...] There is a neat line from the boy in Willoughby to the CEO in Austin. The boy was willing to clean the station because access to the room mattered.
